shortDescription: Shared foundation for the Radius UI suite: one colour set, one card/hover treatment, one scroll widget, one font resolver, and a 268-icon shared art library — shipped once instead of copied into every mod.
body:
## What this mod is

A **library mod**. It adds no defs, no world state, and no Harmony patches. It exists so the
19-mod Radius UI suite draws with one design language instead of 19 forked copies of one.

Design language: flat 2.0, rounded, iOS-like, colour-forward.

Architecture of record: `_dev/RadiusUIFramework/ARCHITECTURE.md` (human-owned). Nothing in
`_dev/` ships.

## Current state

**Texture library: DONE** (imported + duplicate-reviewed). Components: not yet implemented.

## Texture library (268 icons + 12 aliases, 18 categories)

Imported from five source mods — HUD (126), Health Tab (45), Colonist Bar (54), Modern Quest
Menu (23), True RPG Inventory (48). 296 source files → 280 imported → **268 shipped** after a
human duplicate review. All are byte-for-byte copies: no resampling, no recolouring.

All art is namespaced under `Textures/RadiusUI/` because `ContentFinder` returns the
*last-loaded* match, so an un-namespaced sibling in a consumer mod would silently shadow it.
Consumers must delete their local copies, not merely stop referencing them.

Regrouped by **meaning**, not by the per-mod folder accidents the art grew up in. The folder
carries the category, so the prefix is dropped from every name (`Cat_Birthday` →
`Occasion/Birthday`, `MCB_St_Break` → `Status/Break`).

Categories: `Action` 49, `Stat` 32, `Anatomy` 25, `Condition` 22, `Occasion` 18, `Common` 17,
`Slot` 16, `Status` 13, `Weather` 13, `Chrome` 9, `Event` 8, `Marker` 8, `Medical` 8,
`Reminder` 7, `Alert` 7, `Season` 6, `Speed` 5, `Squad` 5.

The whole library is reproducible from source by one script, which also emits the old→new path
map and the alias table. The script is the source of truth; neither generated file is
hand-edited.

### The art is three tiers, not one family

The most important fact for `Palette`/`IconSet` — only tier 1 can be re-themed:

- **Glyphs (~246)** — flat white RGB, all information in the alpha channel. The framework tints
  these via `Palette`/accent at draw time.
- **Illustrations (25, `Anatomy/`)** — rendered beige/cream anatomy with soft shading. Never
  tinted; drawn as-is.
- **Semantic markers (8, `Marker/`)** — colour *is* the meaning (blood, burn, frost, toxic,
  chronic). Mapped to the semantic ramp, never to an arbitrary accent.

`IconSet` must expose tiers 2 and 3 through accessors that do **not** accept a tint, or callers
will silently wash the anatomy art with the user's accent colour.

`Marker/` colours are hand-synced to the palette's semantic ramp — if the ramp changes, those 8
PNGs must be re-authored by hand.

### Aliases are a hard requirement on IconSet

12 names were retired during the duplicate review. Retiring a name never deletes it: an alias
table maps each retired name onto its survivor, and **`IconSet` must expose all 12**, or pilot
migrations break at call sites using the old name. That guarantee is what made the review safe.

Two ordered sets are now partly alias-backed and must still present their full width: `Squad/`
ships 5 files but offers **8** emblem slots; `Reminder/` ships 7 but offers **8** picker slots.

### Kept deliberately against the similarity metric

`Action/LockOpen` and `Action/LockClosed` score 0.927 but are a **state pair** — collapsing them
would leave the UI unable to show locked vs unlocked. A high similarity score is evidence of a
shared design language, never on its own a reason to delete.

`Common/Heart` and `Stat/Heart` both survive: 0.743 to each other, genuinely different weights.

### Deduplication proved the premise

Five apparel-slot icons were shipping **twice today**, bit-identical, in Colonist Bar and True
RPG Inventory. Standardising also surfaced a collision the mod prefixes had hidden: `MCB_Gear`
(a settings cog) vs `MCB_QA_Gear` (a shirt — gear as in apparel), now `Action/Settings` and
`Action/Apparel`.

Slot vocabulary decided: `Boots`, `Helm`, `Torso`, `Legs`, `Belt`, `Weapon`.

Cost: 1.6 MB on disk, ~5.4 MB VRAM as DXT5 + mipmaps.

## Components (specified, not yet built)

- `Tokens/Palette.cs`, `Tokens/Metrics.cs` — pure values, no drawing, no state.
- `Chrome/CardChrome.cs` — the rounded card, border and hover wash.
- `Widgets/FlatScroll.cs` — the suite's scroll view.
- `Icons/IconSet.cs` — typed accessors over the 268 icons, plus the 12 aliases.
- `Text/RadiusFont.cs` — framework-owned font resolution. Centralising this is the single
  largest memory win available, because `Font.CreateDynamicFontFromOSFont` builds a glyph atlas
  per caller.
- `Settings/` — `RadiusTheme`, `RadiusThemeSettings`, `RadiusFrameworkMod`. Theme is owned
  globally so the user picks an accent once; a consumer may register a local override.

## Decisions already fixed

- Hard dependency model. Harmony is declared for load-order chaining only
  (`Harmony → Framework → consumers`); the framework applies no patches and never calls into it.
- Pilot consumers, in order: **HUD**, **Health Tab** (dropping the Modern brand), **Colonist
  Bar** last — it has no palette file at all (75 inline `Color` literals across 12 files) and is
  a true per-frame drawer, making it the strongest proof and the slowest migration.
- Quest Menu and True RPG Inventory are **not** consumers; their art was taken as library stock
  for later use.
